text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Centre Union decided on Saturday to back former US environmental bureaucrat Valdas Admakus to run in presidential elections expected at the end of the year. It still remains unclear whether the electoral commission will be allow Adamkus to run since the constitution requires presidential candidates to live in Lithuania for at least three years.
- Asta Vyshniauskaite, 20, was elected Miss Lithuania 97 on Friday night.
- Lithuanian finance minister Algirdas Shemeta said that the State Commercial Bank, slated for privatisation, will be sold for 400 litas.
- The Agricultural Bank decided to boost its share capital by 42.875 million litas to 173 million litas to meet the capital adequacy ratio requirements of the Bank of Lithuania.
- An explosion hit a shop in Kaunas on Sunday. The shopkeeper alleged it was the work of his competitors.
- TV 3 channel, acquired by Swedish Modern Times Group, started broadcasting in Lithuania on Sunday.
- Enviroment protection minister Imantas Lazdinis has sucessfully undergone heart surgery.
- The official reserves of the Bank of Lithuania in May were $883.3 million, the highest since 1993.
- Inflation in Lithuania in May rose to 0.8 percent from 0.3 percent in April because of the increase in fuel prices.
- Mazeikiu Nafta refined 583,000 tonnes of crude in April and the company's plans to refine six million tonnes of crude this year are looking realistic.
- Lithuanian companies eye the Ukrainian market. Eighty companies will participate in the fair Lithuania offers in Kiev on June 12-14.
- Lithuania's investment agency forecasts that foreign direct investments in the country will be $850 million at the end of 1997.
